Information Ecosystem Theme Team Update
[contact omitted] Matthew Baker Thursday, November 18, 2021 at 4:23:20 PM Eastern Standard Time
To: [contact omitted] Diana Parzik, [contact omitted] Daniel Sabet, [contact omitted] Jared Ford, [contact omitted]
Joshua Machleder, [contact omitted] Lisa Poggiali, [contact omitted] Michael McNulty, [contact omitted] Morgan
Holmes
HI All,
Thanks to all those who attended yesterday's conversation. We discussed the feedback from the DRG Cadre as well as
ensuring the question remains open and broad to not second guess the results. We wanted to suggest the following
question formulation with three subquestions. We have also updated the document with a revised rationale statement.
• What factors influence the information ecosystem related to disinformation, misinformation and malinformation?
• What factors influence the susceptibility to believing and sharing disinformation, misinformation and
malinformation?
• What factors influence the supply of disinformation, misinformation and malinformation?
• What enabling environmental factors influence both?
Can you please share any final suggested edits by Monday November 22nd COB. I will concurrently work on a draft
scope and invite you to a scoping discussion after Thanksgiving.
Many thanks again.
Best,
Matt
Matthew Baker (he/him/his),

Hi Matt -- just wanted to chime in here, since unfortunately I wasn't able to be present for the discussion; but Lisa and l
had a side chat. We should be mindful that Global Engagement Center at State produces an index (I believe it's Global
Disinformation Resilience Index) that looks at a range of factors to understand a country's susceptibility. That is somewhat
similar to the factors listed here (specifically when talking about the environment level/country level, but *not* the
individual level. I am certain that my colleagues on this distro have been exposed to that tool, so | just want to be certain
that we incorporate the learnings from that and are not duplicative of existing efforts.
Best, Josh

[contact omitted] Lisa Poggiali Friday, November 19, 2021 at 5:27:01 PM Eastern Standard Time
To: [contact omitted] Matthew Baker
Cc: [contact omitted] Diana Parzik, [contact omitted] Joshua Machleder, [contact omitted] Daniel Sabet,
[contact omitted] Jared Ford, [contact omitted] Michael McNulty, [contact omitted] Morgan Holmes
Hi Matt and others,
I took a stab at trying to make the question more concrete -- it seemed to be getting so abstract it was hard to see how
someone would start answering it -- and also capture Diana and Josh's points.
I think the addition of resilience captures that we're interested in both mis/mal/disinformation and the information
ecosystem at large. I added the specific factors and dynamics to signal what existing research has shown us about the
influences on information ecosystems. Would suggest Diana and Josh review since they are up on the existing literature.
Thanks to Matt for corralling all of us thus far!
best,
Lisa
On Fri, Nov 19, 2021 at 5:25 PM Matthew Baker <[contact omitted]> wrote:
Thanks for all the comments and reflections. I did a quick look but wanted to flag that at this point we should ideally
focus on the first - prioritized - learning question. The remaining questions are here for reference and of course we can
improve upon.
I am going to take note of these points too as we transition to thinking of scoping research as these points should be
considered when we scope and researchers eventually craft a concept.
Many thanks.
On Fri, Nov 19, 2021 at 2:28 PM Diana Parzik <[contact omitted]> wrote:
Matt-
Thanks for pulling this together, I think we're on the home stretch. The GEC's program is the Digital Disinfo Index
(DDI) and I'm happy to pull folks together so we can integrate that work into this research.
I added a few comments below Josh's in the questions, mostly minor tweaks (e.g. including mal-information where
we just reference mis- and dis) and also language on 'building resilience'. In the IIR R&D meeting this morning, Mary
Beth and Brian intentionally flagged the NSM LOE on 'building resilience' and the research gap we have in that
space. I think this is mostly covered by question 3.
Also, I put some comments in about further clarification for question 5 on 'non-democratic actors'.
Thanks,
Diana
